chosen_hypothesis.statement: An S-shaped lid-driven cavity cross-section will generate steady secondary Dean-like counter-rotating vortex pairs at Re = 500, reducing the 90%-mixing length of a passive scalar by more than 40% relative to a rectangular cavity of equal volume driven at the same lid speed.
chosen_hypothesis.rationale: Ref. 2205.08127 demonstrates that S-shaped microchannel geometry induces chaotic advection through secondary vortex formation even in purely laminar flows; the same curvature-driven centrifugal mechanism should produce persistent transverse vortices inside a lid-driven cavity and dramatically increase interfacial stretching.

experiment_spec.title: S-shaped cavity secondary-vortex onset at Re = 500
experiment_spec.objective: Determine whether a 2D S-shaped staircase lid-driven cavity at Re = 500 produces secondary in-plane recirculations strong enough to raise the volume-averaged velocity magnitude above 0.35 m/s, a level exceeding the expected single-vortex rectangular baseline by at least 10–40 %.

qoi.name: vol_avg_speed
qoi.definition: Volume-averaged magnitude of the steady-state velocity field, (1/V) integral_V |U| dV, evaluated over the full cavity cross-section. Additional counter-rotating recirculation cells contribute additive kinetic energy throughout the domain and are expected to drive this metric measurably above the single-vortex rectangular baseline, making it a proxy for secondary vortex presence and intensity.
qoi.how_extracted: Substrate qoi request: field=U, operation=volAverage, component=mag at the latest written time step.

success_criterion.statement: At s_amplitude_fraction = 0.30 the vol_avg_speed exceeds 0.35 m/s. The rectangular baseline at Re = 500, U_lid = 1.0 m/s is estimated at 0.25–0.32 m/s based on known single-vortex cavity scaling; exceeding 0.35 m/s therefore requires a 10–40 % enhancement consistent with secondary vortex formation driven by S-shaped curvature.

regime.notes: Re = 500 is 2.5x above the validated substrate envelope (spike at Re = 200) but remains deeply laminar; cavity-flow turbulence onset is typically Re > 7000, so the 2D laminar assumption is physically sound. The S-shaped cavity is realised as a four-block staircase: lower chamber (x in [0, W], y in [0, H/2]) plus upper chamber (x in [-alpha*W, (1-alpha)*W], y in [H/2, H]), sharing an interior fluid interface of width (1-alpha)*W at y = H/2, plus right dead-end nub (x in [(1-alpha)*W, W], y in [0, H/2]) and left dead-end nub (x in [-alpha*W, 0], y in [H/2, H]); total cross-sectional area = W*H for all alpha, equal-volume condition holds exactly. Multi-block blockMesh for non-rectangular topology is unproven on this substrate and flagged for the fidelity gate. In 2D the solver cannot produce true 3D Dean vortex pairs; what forms are in-plane secondary recirculations mechanistically analogous to counter-rotating Dean-like pairs but not identical. The hypothesis QoI (90%-mixing length of a passive scalar) is NOT extractable: the incompressible laminar solver carries no scalar-transport physics and writes no concentration field. vol_avg_speed is used as a velocity-field proxy for secondary vortex intensity; no quantitative bridge to the 40% mixing-length reduction claim is available with this substrate, and feasibility of the full mixing-length assertion is a downstream fidelity-gate judgment. The threshold of 0.35 m/s is estimated from the expected baseline; its validity is uncertain at the unvalidated Re = 500 operating point.

mini_experiment.expected_observation: Run 1 (alpha = 0, rectangular) converges to a single Burggraf-type primary vortex; vol_avg_speed expected near 0.25–0.32 m/s. Run 2 (alpha = 0.15) shows the lower and upper sub-chambers beginning to develop weakly coupled recirculations fed by the S-throat; vol_avg_speed modestly above Run 1. Run 3 (alpha = 0.30) exhibits distinct secondary recirculations in each sub-chamber and a strong redirection jet at the S-throat; vol_avg_speed should exceed Run 1 by at least 10% and ideally surpass the 0.35 m/s threshold, providing preliminary evidence for the secondary-vortex mechanism.

full_experiment.design: Sweep s_amplitude_fraction over six evenly spaced values (0.00, 0.06, 0.12, 0.18, 0.24, 0.30) at fixed Re = 500, lid_velocity = 1.0 m/s, kinematic_viscosity = 0.002 m^2/s, cavity_width = 1.0 m, cavity_height = 1.0 m, mesh_cells_per_meter = 64. Geometry: four-block blockMesh staircase S-shape as described in regime.notes; the moving lid is the top wall of the upper chamber (y = 1.0 m, x in [-alpha, 1-alpha] m) at +1.0 m/s in x; all other walls stationary no-slip. Solve with simpleFoam (steady incompressible) to convergence (all residuals < 1e-3). Mesh-independence check: add six additional runs at mesh_cells_per_meter = 32 and 96 for alpha in {0.00, 0.15, 0.30}, bracketing coarseness effects on vol_avg_speed. Total: 6 sweep + 6 mesh-independence = 12 runs. Analysis: plot vol_avg_speed vs alpha to identify the onset s_amplitude_fraction above which secondary recirculations produce a statistically distinct break in the curve, and compare the alpha = 0.30 value against the alpha = 0.00 baseline to evaluate the success criterion.

fidelity_verdict.label: refine
fidelity_verdict.rationale: The 2D laminar solver genuinely handles this cavity-class physics and directly computes vol_avg_speed, but it is being extrapolated well past its validated envelope (Re 2.5x higher, an unproven multi-block staircase mesh, no mesh-independence at the S-throat) so it yields a reliable predicted screen, not a reality-confirmed answer.
fidelity_verdict.right_instrument: cavity_2d (used as a screening filter; survivors require mesh-independence confirmation and real-world/human validation at Re=500)
